result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the Bethe Hessian matrix of an undirected graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L48951-L49003){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix( r=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bethe Hessian matrix](/assets/graphs/bethe-hessian-matrix.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node graph with degree badges and its Bethe Hessian at the default r = 1.67 (32 / 12 - 1, from the degrees). Each edge gives -r = -1.67 and the diagonal (accent) holds r² - 1 + degree: 3.78 for A, 4.78 for B, C and D, and 2.78 for E. At r = 1 it would be the Laplacian." width="100%"} The Bethe Hessian `H(r) = (r² - 1) I - r A + D` (Saade, Krzakala & Zdeborová, 2014) is a regularized Laplacian built for community detection in large sparse networks, where ordinary spectral methods break down: there, the number of its negative eigenvalues estimates the number of communities, and the corresponding eigenvectors reveal them. At `r = 1` it is exactly the Laplacian. The default `r` is the average excess degree `Σ d² / Σ d - 1` (unweighted degrees), as in NetworkX's `bethe_hessian_matrix()`; Saade et al. recommend its square root, which you can pass explicitly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The regularizer. If `None` (default), uses `Σ d² / Σ d - 1`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the adjacency and degree terms use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or `r=` is omitted on a graph without edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} At `r = 1` the Bethe Hessian is the Laplacian: ::: {#cb15611a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4) bethe, nodes = path.bethe_hessian_matrix(r=1) bethe, bethe == path.laplacian_matrix()[0] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[1.0, -1.0, 0.0, 0.0], [-1.0, 2.0, -1.0, 0.0], [0.0, -1.0, 2.0, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, -1.0, 1.0]], True) ``` ::: :::
